name: overview
prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. New textbook concept illustration, wide 3:1 landscape banner, about 2048 by 683. Input images are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY: the retro PC desk and room illustrations from a user-supplied pixel wallpaper collection. Borrow visual technique, not the exact room arrangement. Authentic late-1980s/1990s Japanese PC adventure-game background art: strong limited 16-color-like palette, chunky visible square pixels, black/navy pixel outlines, checkerboard dithering for shadows, flat cel-like color regions, crisp sprite silhouettes. Cyan, periwinkle, plum, magenta accents, warm pale-beige CRT housings. NOT smooth modern illustration, NOT painterly, NOT isometric miniature diorama, no anti-aliased 3D rendering.

Scene: one believable security training office shown with a FIXED level camera and consistent one-point perspective, naturally composed as left/center/right zones. LEFT: unmistakable fictional attacker, dark charcoal hooded sweatshirt with muted crimson accent, seated with BACK OF HEAD AND BACK FACING CAMERA; no face visible. He types on a real keyboard at a beige old desktop PC and thick CRT facing away from him toward the camera enough that only the attacker-side screen naturally visible. Keep monitor, keyboard, hands and desk physically connected and plausible; the monitor screen faces the attacker. CENTER: equipment zone with a compact half-height 19-inch rack with stacked horizontal servers, separate flat network security appliance with two rows of ports, neatly routed patch cables. RIGHT: defender, alert short-haired young woman in teal office shirt with simple headset, seated BEHIND her desk FACING CAMERA in natural front-three-quarter view, face and both shoulders clearly visible. Her monitor is on the desk BETWEEN her and the camera; show ONLY ITS SOLID BEIGE BACK and ventilation slots, not its screen. Keyboard lies on her side of the monitor, hands naturally typing. The screen faces her, not the viewer. Never show the back of a monitor as a display.

Place all characters and furniture entirely inside frame, no cut-off heads. Use straightforward believable room geometry and grounded furniture, NO floating papers, NO giant magnifying glasses, NO forced twisted body, NO double-sided screens, NO impossible see-through objects. Main objects large enough to read on a 15 cm print banner; omit excess plants and decoration. The lighting makes attacker side deeper plum and defender side clear cyan but keep one coherent room. No text, letters, digits, brand logos, UI panels, captions or arrows; Korean labels will be typeset separately. All invented scene, not actual software screenshot.
role: 생성형 개념 삽화. 실제 실행 화면이나 네트워크 배치도가 아님.

name: sqli
prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. New book concept illustration, wide 3:1 landscape banner. Reference 1 is the APPROVED CHARACTER/STYLE/CAMERA guide: dark hooded attacker seen from behind on the left, short-haired teal-shirt headset defender whose face is visible on right. Reference 2 is the pixel-rendering style guide from a retro game image collection. Maintain the same cast, visual pixel density, limited cyan/periwinkle/plum/magenta/pale-beige palette, dark pixel outlines, flat cel areas, visible square pixels and checkerboard dithering. Authentic old PC adventure-game graphics, NOT modern smooth art, NOT isometric miniature cutaway, no painterly shading.

Physical perspective is crucial: one fixed ordinary eye-level camera, one consistent perspective across the room. Attacker's BACK and back of hood face the camera, never show his face; he types on a real keyboard in front of a CRT whose SCREEN faces HIM. Defender sits on the far side of her desk facing toward the camera, front-three-quarter face clearly visible above and beside her monitor. We see ONLY the back/side housing of her monitor, its screen faces her. Hands stay naturally at her keyboard on her side of the monitor. No double-sided screens, no floating software panels, no transparent monitors, no bent impossible chairs or twisted bodies. Do not force screen content into view. No letters, digits, labels, brand marks, arrows or legible software UI: explanations will be typeset separately. Original invented concept scene, not screenshot. Large clear silhouettes suited to 15 cm print width. Maintain grounded desk/equipment geometry. Vary layout and equipment to suit scene; do not clone the same rack in all images. Scene: Left, rear-view hooded attacker at a compact late-1980s horizontal desktop PC with bulky CRT composing a suspicious web request; screen has sparse abstract magenta code bars, not readable text. Center, a networking bench containing a LOW flat standalone firewall/security appliance with two neat rows of ports and indicator lamps; beside it a separate upright web server tower in dark grey, cable routed naturally between them. No airport security conveyor, paper sorting metaphor or guard at a checkpoint. Right, front-facing teal-shirt defender with her recognizable face visible, seated behind a DIFFERENT beige CRT with its back to viewer; she studies the logs on the unseen screen. A single room with left plum and right cyan lighting, little clutter, no gratuitous plants. Center hardware is large and easily distinguished from both desktop computers. Show attempted attack and observation, not explosions or proof of successful breach.
